steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: Language analysis examines how writers choose and use words, phrases and literary devices to create specific effects on the reader. | Alliteration: Repetition of consonant sounds for emphasis or musicality. "The slippery snake slithered silently." | Onomatopoeia: Words that sound like what they describe. "Crash, bang, hiss, whisper." | Sibilance: Repeated 's' sounds creating a hissing effect. "The soft, silky snake slid through the grass."

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: What is the difference between a metaphor and a simile? | What does PEEL stand for? | Why should you avoid writing "this makes the reader want to read on"?

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Alliteration, Onomatopoeia, Sibilance, and one past-paper question.
